newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia reports attack by Somalia-based militants.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia reports attack by Somalia-based militants.

text.p: Ethiopia said on Tuesday its defence forces had repulsed a cross-border attack by Somali-based Moslem fundamentalists, killing or wounding more than 100 attackers.

The ministry of defence said in a statement carried by the state-run Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) that its forces "killed or wounded over 100 (members of a) multi-national fundamentalist extermist group who tried to cross into the Ethiopian territory in an attempt to launch an attack on the town of Dolow".
"Ninteen members of the multi-national fundamentalist group killed during the offensive were of Arab origin from different Arab countries," it said.
Ethiopian television showed on Tuesday night bodies strewn on the battleground.
The statement did not mention casualties on the government side and did not say when the fighting took place.
It was the first word from Addis Ababa on fighting against members of the al-Ittihad al-Islami (Islamic Union) but did not refer to any fighting inside Somalia.
Aid workers, security sources and al-Ittihad in Mogadishu say Ethiopian troops have advanced into Somalia seizing a number villages.

A security source said on Tuesday Ethiopian troops were six km (four miles) from the village of Beled Hawo on the road to the fundamentalist stronghold of Luq, more than 100 km (60 miles) from the Ethiopian border.
Al-Ittihad said its fighters made a "tactical retreat" on Monday night after inflicting heavy losses on the Ethiopians.
The Ethiopian defence ministry warned that Ethiopia was prepared to deal a crushing blow to the group.
"Ethiopia will not tolerate the futile attempt by the group to impose its belief on neighbouring countries. It is determined to deal a crushing blow to such attempts in future too."
Ethiopia said in August that its troops killed more than 230 al-Ittihad fighters and destroyed three of their camps in an incursion into Somalia that month.
